content.Quality indicators: There is a lack of implementation studies evaluating whether prospectively monitoring and reporting ESC QIs for ACS improve clinical outcomes. Implementation studies evaluating a quality of care programme based on the evaluation of ESC QIs for ACS are recommended.
content.General: Patients included in clinical trials represent a relatively small proportion of real-life patients. Recommendation: Conduct clinical trials that enrol more representative patient populations (e.g. pragmatic clinical trials).
content.Ongoing trials: Ongoing trials addressing some of these gaps in evidence are presented in the Supplementary data online.
Abbreviations: MINOCA: myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries
content.Sex differences: There are currently no data supporting differential management of ACS based on sex. Several studies report that women presenting with ACS are treated differently than men — including being less likely to receive ICA, timely revascularization, cardiac rehabilitation, and secondary prevention medications.
